name: Georg Heinrich von Görtz
summary:
Georg Heinrich von Görtz (1668-1719) was a German baron and statesman who played a significant role in Swedish politics during the late reign of King Charles XII.

As a diplomat, von Görtz negotiated several key treaties with European powers, including the Treaty of Stockholm (1710), which helped to secure Sweden's borders against Russian expansion. He also served as a member of the Swedish Riksdag, where he advocated for reforms and modernization.

Von Görtz's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of his diplomatic efforts, particularly with regards to Sweden's relations with its Nordic neighbors. His commitment to reform and modernization helped pave the way for Sweden's emergence as a major European power in the early 18th century.

Despite his significant contributions to Swedish politics, von Görtz remains somewhat overshadowed by other prominent figures of the era, such as King Charles XII and Adolf Fredrik.

The 1719 Treaty of Stockholm is often cited as one of the most important agreements of the Swedish Age of Liberty, marking a turning point in Sweden's relations with its European neighbors.
